extracted.intended_audience: persons and entities filing applications or other filings with the Federal Communications Commission (applicants, permittees, licensees), payors, and FCC Financial Operations/processing staff
extracted.subtask_short: fcc fee payment and filing rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing payment, forms, filing locations, refunds, exemptions, adjustments, penalties, and schedules for fees and regulatory charges under 47 CFR Part 1 (FCC). Intended to guide applicants and FCC staff on compliant submission and processing of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of charges (§ 1.1111)
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedule of fees for applications and other filings lists those applications and other filings that must be accompanied by an FCC Form 159, 'Remittance Advice' or the electronic version (FCC Form 159-E) generated by the Commission's on-line filing and payment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may use the Commission's online filing systems and fee payment module (URLs provided). Applications and filings not submitted in accordance with these instructions will be returned as unprocessable. Simultaneous submission of fee forms does not apply to fees with established billing processes (§ 1.1121). Applications returned for additional information/corrections do not require an additional fee unless the new information increases the original fee; original fee forfeited if resubmitted late. If staff changes application status increasing the fee due, the applicant will be billed for the remainder (§ 1.1118(b)). Special procedures may apply to tariff filings (note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of payment (§ 1.1112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual and multiple year regulatory fees must be paid electronically. Other fee payments should be by check, cashier's check, or money order in U.S. dollars drawn on a U.S. financial institution and payable to the Federal Communications Commission, or by Visa, MasterCard, American Express, or Discover credit card (no other cards accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit card payments require the credit card section of FCC Form 159 completed. Cash discouraged and not the Commission's responsibility if mailed. Personal/corporate checks older than six months or postdated checks not accepted; third-party checks not accepted. Payers are encouraged to submit payments electronically; Bureau/Office guides announce electronic procedures. Payer is responsible to ensure proper electronic payment procedures; wire transfers must follow Bureau/Office fee guide instructions. One payment instrument and FCC Form 159 required per application/filing (exceptions: multiple money orders allowed where single money order maximum is exceeded). The Commission may require cashier's checks for payors with prior payment instrument failures and will notify in writing if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic payment requirement for annual and multiple-year regulatory fees (§ 1.1112(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual and multiple year regulatory fee payments shall be submitted by online ACH payment, online Visa/MasterCard/American Express/Discover credit card payment, or wire transfer denominated in U.S. dollars drawn on a U.S. financial institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other form of payment for regulatory fees (e.g., paper checks) will be rejected and returned to the payor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing locations and package submission (§ 1.1113)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and other filings, with attached fees and FCC Form 159, must be submitted to the specific locations/addresses set forth in §§ 1.1102–1.1109 (with exceptions noted in the section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tariff filings to the Secretary, FCC; bills for collection paid at Commission's lockbox bank and must include the bill reference number; petitions for reconsideration or applications for review of fee decisions must include the required fee. Except where provided, all materials must be submitted as one package—the Commission will not match fees/forms submitted at different times/locations. For Wireless Radio Services via ULS and for MVCTS/CARS via COALS, payments may be electronic or manual but manual payments must include the application file number or generated FCC Form 159 and must be received no later than 10 days after receipt of application in the electronic system or the application will be dismissed/forfeited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionality of Commission or staff authorizations (§ 1.1114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any instrument of authorization granted by the Commission or staff will be conditioned upon final payment of the applicable fee(s) and timely payment of bills issued by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final payment not made prior to grant, the application may be dismissed, lose processing place, and not receive nunc pro tunc treatment if resubmitted after deadline. If payment fails after grant, the Commission will rescind the authorization, notify the grantee, and not permit nunc pro tunc treatment; the grantee must immediately cease operations. Deferred payment or billing-based processing is conditioned on final payment by prescribed dates; failure results in dismissal or rescission. Staff will request delinquent fees in writing and may withhold action or dismiss if payment/arrangements not made within 30 days of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return or refund of charges (§ 1.1115)
rubrics_metrics.description: All refunds will be issued to the payer named on the FCC Form 159; the full amount of any fee submitted will be returned or refunded under specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated refund circumstances include: when no fee is required; when processing staff determines an insufficient fee within 30 days and the filing is dismissed; applicant cannot meet age requirement; Commission adopts rules or law/treaty rendering the application/grant useless; when a waiver is granted; overpayment refunds only if $10 or more; when a new/modified facilities application is not timely filed within a filing window. Additional specific refund rules for first-come, first-served Media Services and space station applicants are provided (procedural conditions and timing). Comparative hearings are no longer required (paragraph (b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: General exemptions to charges (§ 1.1116)
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee shall be required for certain specified categories of applications/filings unless otherwise qualified in the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions include: applications solely to modify existing authorization to comply with new Commission/Federal agency requirements (unless additional action requested); government entities or nonprofit entities in Special Emergency/Public Safety Radio Services (IRS Determination Letter required for nonprofit status); noncommercial educational (NCE) broadcast stations (FM/TV and certain AM operations); radio services used in conjunction with NCE broadcasts; organizations receiving Public Broadcasting Fund funding for NCE use; translators/low power TV proposing NCE service that later show NTIA or other funding to qualify for refund; governmental entities defined broadly; restricted radiotelephone operator permits used solely with exempt facilities. Applicants claiming exemptions must certify eligibility via cover letter unless the FCC form requests the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to charges (§ 1.1117)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schedule of Charges will be reviewed by the Commission on Oct 1, 1999 and every two years thereafter, with adjustments based on changes in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments apply against base fees as enacted/amended by Congress. Individual fees will not be adjusted until net CPI-U change equals at least $5 for fees under $100 or 5% or more for fees $100 or greater. All fees adjusted upward to the next $5 increment. Adjustments under these procedures will not be subject to notice-and-comment rulemaking or petitions for reconsideration; requests for modification limited to correcting arithmetic errors during adjustment cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for late or insufficient payments (§ 1.1118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings with defective fee submissions will be dismissed if the defect is discovered within 30 calendar days; defective fees may be corrected by resubmission with the correct fee; insufficient fees discovered after 30 days will be billed and subject to penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When billed, a penalty equal to 25% of the amount due is added to each bill for applications accompanied by insufficient or no fees discovered after 30 days; any Commission action taken prior to timely payment is contingent and subject to rescission. Deferrals granted are billed plus 25% charge. Failure to submit fees after notice is subject to collection including interest, penalties, and full cost of collection under the Debt Collection Improvement Act (31 U.S.C. 3711 et seq.), and collection processes may proceed concurrently with other sanctions. For filing timeliness, resubmission date is considered the filing date except where bank error is evidenced by bank affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions and applications for review; waivers and deferrals (§ 1.1119)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees may be waived or deferred where good cause is shown and waiver/deferral would promote the public interest. Requests only considered when received from applicants acting with respect to their own applications; class-wide requests not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions/requests acted on by the Managing Director with concurrence of the General Counsel; filings within the scope of fee rules must be filed as a separate pleading and clearly marked for the Managing Director or they will not be considered. Requests for deferral due to financial hardship must include supporting documentation. Deferrals are granted for up to six months. Applicants seeking waivers must submit the waiver request with the application, required fee and FCC Form 159 (or a request for deferral); waiver requests lacking these materials will be dismissed and submitted fees will be returned if a waiver is granted. Fee waivers based on financial hardship are subject to § 1.1166(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Error claims and challenges (§ 1.1120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may challenge in writing a staff determination of an insufficient fee or delinquent debt; challenges to delinquency must be accompanied by proof that the fee was paid/waived/deferred or by the required payment and any assessment penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims addressed to Financial Operations (address provided) or emailed to ARINQUIRIES@fcc.gov. Actions by Financial Operations are subject to reconsideration/review provisions of §§ 1.106 and 1.115, except reconsideration/review is available only where the applicant has made the full and proper payment of the underlying fee. Petitions for reconsideration/applications for review by applicants who have not made full payment will be dismissed; if the fee payment fails while Commission is considering the matter, the petition/application will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing procedures (§ 1.1121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fees (e.g., International Telecommunications Settlements, Accounting and Audits Field Audits, Review of Arrest Audits) should not be paid with the filing; for some urgent or emergency Special Temporary Authority requests, the fee should not be paid with the Bureau/Office filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these cases the Commission will determine the appropriate fee and bill the filer. The bill will specify the amount, payment due date, and address for payment. See also § 1.1113 for related filing location/payment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to prescribe and collect regulatory fees (§ 1.1151)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to impose and collect regulatory fees is contained in section 9 of the Communications Act, as amended (47 U.S.C. 159).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority directs the Commission to prescribe and collect annual regulatory fees to recover the cost of carrying out Commission functions; the section citation and legislative references are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of annual regulatory fees for wireless radio services (§ 1.1152)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 sets forth annual regulatory fee amounts for exclusive use wireless radio services (per license) including land mobile, microwave, shared use land mobile, rural radio, marine coast, aviation ground/aircraft/ship, CMRS cellular/messaging (per unit), broadband radio service, and local multipoint distribution service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific dollar amounts and distinctions for new/renew/mod and electronic filing vs other filing modes are provided in the table. Some listed fees are noted as standard fees to be paid in accordance with § 1.1157(b). The table is dated (89 FR 78508, Sept. 25, 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of annual regulatory fees and filing locations for mass media services (§ 1.1153)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 provides fee amounts for mass media services (radio AM/FM by class and population bands, FM construction permits, TV digital construction permits and fee factor per population, low power TV/Class A/translator & booster fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are specified by station class and population tiers for AM and FM, with construction permit fees and TV fee factors noted. The table includes effective date citation (89 FR 78509, Sept. 25, 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of annual regulatory charges for common carrier services (§ 1.1154)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 lists fees for certain radio facilities (e.g., microwave domestic public fixed) and carrier fees such as interstate telephone service provider fees (per revenues) and toll-free number fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes electronic filing designations and references to underlying FCC forms (e.g., FCC Form 601 & 159). Specific rates and formulations (e.g., .00542 per interstate and international end-user revenues) are provided; effective date citation included (89 FR 78510, Sept. 25, 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of regulatory fees for cable television services (§ 1.1155)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 sets forth regulatory fees for cable television services including Cable Television Relay Service and Cable TV System/IPTV/DBS per-subscriber fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific dollar amounts provided (e.g., $1,825 for Cable Television Relay Service; $1.27 per subscriber for Cable TV System/IPTV and DBS). Effective date citation included (89 FR 78510, Sept. 25, 2024).
